name: ZITLAS Masala Oats Khichdi
description: Rolled oats cooked khichdi-style with toor dal and vegetables in one pot — a savoury oats format for people who dislike sweet porridge oats.
ingredients: Mustard seeds, turmeric, curry leaves — 3 g
instructions: Rinse toor dal and pressure cook with vegetables and turmeric for 2 whistles until soft.
Dry-roast the oats separately for 2 minutes until lightly toasted.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, add the cooked dal-vegetable mix and the roasted oats with a little water.
Simmer 3-4 minutes until the oats soften into a khichdi consistency.
Serve hot.
why_it_works: Savoury format avoids the usual sweet-oats fatigue
One-pot, mostly hands-off cooking
Dal brings meaningfully more protein than oats alone

name: ZITLAS Besan Paneer Roll
description: A besan crepe rolled (not folded) around a dry-spiced paneer filling — a different construction from a folded chilla, closer to a kathi roll.
instructions: Whisk besan and water into a thin, dosa-like batter.
Pan-cook a thin round on a hot tawa, similar to a dosa rather than a thick chilla.
Separately dry-toss paneer with onion and chaat masala (no extra oil needed here).
Lay the filling along one edge of the thin besan crepe and roll tightly kathi-roll style.
Slice and serve.
why_it_works: Thin-roll format is a genuinely different eating experience from a folded chilla
Dry-tossed filling keeps added fat lower
Portable once rolled

name: ZITLAS Egg Curry with Multigrain Roti
description: Boiled eggs simmered in a light onion-tomato curry, served with a multigrain roti — a curry format rather than the usual bhurji or omelette.
instructions: Knead the multigrain atta into a dough and roll into rotis; roast on a tawa and keep warm.
Heat oil, saute onion until golden, add ginger-garlic paste and tomato, cook until pulpy.
Add garam masala and a little water to form a light gravy; simmer 5 minutes.
Halve the boiled eggs and add them into the gravy, simmering 2-3 minutes.
Serve hot with the rotis.
why_it_works: Curry format is a genuinely different way to eat eggs from bhurji or omelette
Multigrain roti adds fiber the usual white-flour roti lacks
Filling, complete meal-style breakfast

name: ZITLAS Moong Dal Tikki Sandwich
description: Boiled and mashed moong dal shaped into pan-fried tikkis and sandwiched in toasted bread — a patty-in-sandwich format distinct from a wrap or roll.
ingredients: Moong dal, boiled and mashed — 100 g
Red chilli powder, coriander powder — 3 g
instructions: Mash the boiled moong dal with onion and spices into a firm mixture.
Shape into a flat tikki.
Pan-fry in oil until crisp on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Toast the bread and sandwich the tikki inside.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Patty format holds together better than loose dal for a sandwich
Cheap, filling, and genuinely different texture from a wrap
Good option for people who find rolls hard to eat on the move

name: ZITLAS Peanut Curd Dip with Veg Sticks
description: A thick spiced peanut-curd dip served with raw steamed vegetable sticks — an unusual dipping-format breakfast that's essentially no-cook.
instructions: Whisk curd with crushed peanuts and roasted cumin powder into a thick dip.
Cut carrot and cucumber into sticks.
Arrange the vegetable sticks around the dip.
Eat by dipping — no utensils beyond a bowl needed.
why_it_works: Genuinely no-cook, unlike most vegetable-based breakfasts
High raw-vegetable volume for very few calories
Different eating format keeps breakfast varied

name: ZITLAS Soya Frankie Roll
description: A Mumbai street-food-style frankie: spiced soya granules rolled inside a lightly charred wheat roti with onion and a tangy sauce.
instructions: Roll out the atta into a roti and roast on a tawa until slightly charred at the edges.
Separately, saute the rehydrated soya granules with pav bhaji masala until well coated and slightly dry.
Spread green and tamarind chutney on the roti, add the soya filling and sliced onion.
Roll tightly frankie-style and wrap the bottom in paper.
Serve immediately while the roti is warm.
why_it_works: Street-food frankie format is distinct from a paratha or kathi roll
Two chutneys give a genuinely different flavour profile from other rolls in the database
Good grab-and-eat option for a commute

name: ZITLAS Kuttu Pancake with Curd
description: A fasting-day-style buckwheat (kuttu) flour pancake, pan-cooked and served with plain curd — a gluten-free option using a flour rarely seen outside Navratri cooking.
instructions: Whisk kuttu flour with water, rock salt and finely chopped green chilli into a thick batter.
Heat oil on a tawa, pour the batter and spread into a small thick pancake (kuttu doesn't spread thin easily).
Cook 2-3 minutes per side until firm and lightly browned.
Serve with a side of plain curd.
why_it_works: Genuinely gluten-free flour choice, unusual outside fasting contexts
Distinct nutty flavour keeps the breakfast rotation varied
Curd on the side adds protein the flour itself lacks

name: ZITLAS Egg-Coated Paratha
description: A whole wheat paratha dipped in beaten egg and pan-cooked so the egg forms a coating on the outside, rather than being stuffed inside — an anda-paratha street-food style.
instructions: Knead atta into a dough, roll out and dry-roast a plain paratha until about 70% done.
Beat the egg with onion, pepper and chilli flakes.
Dip the half-cooked paratha into the beaten egg, coating one side.
Return to the tawa, egg-side down, with a little oil, and cook until the egg sets and browns.
Flip briefly, then serve.
why_it_works: Coating technique is genuinely different construction from a stuffed paratha
Familiar street-food format (anda paratha) most people already enjoy
One dough, one egg, one pan

name: ZITLAS Sprout Paneer Tikki
description: Mashed sprouted moong combined with crumbled paneer, shaped into pan-fried patties — a distinct patty format pairing two protein sources directly rather than as filling.
ingredients: Coriander, green chilli, cumin powder — 5 g
instructions: Coarsely grind the moong sprouts (don't puree fully — keep some texture).
Mix with crumbled paneer, onion, coriander, green chilli and cumin powder.
Shape into 3-4 small tikkis.
Pan-fry in oil until golden on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Serve with mint chutney.
why_it_works: Two proteins combined directly into one patty, not one as filling for the other
Notably high protein density for the calorie cost
Good make-ahead-and-fry option

name: ZITLAS Rajgira Milk Porridge
description: Amaranth (rajgira) flour cooked into a warm milk porridge with dates — a fasting-day grain used here as a regular sweet breakfast porridge.
instructions: Whisk rajgira flour into a little cold milk first to avoid lumps.
Heat the remaining milk in a pan, add the flour mixture and stir continuously.
Simmer 6-8 minutes until thickened, stirring often.
Stir in chopped dates and cardamom powder, cook 2 more minutes, and serve warm.
why_it_works: Amaranth has a notably different mineral and fiber profile from wheat or rava porridges
Naturally gluten-free
Dates sweeten without refined sugar

name: ZITLAS Chana Sundal Bowl
description: A South Indian temple-style tempered chickpea sundal, eaten as a warm protein bowl rather than the usual evening snack serving.
ingredients: Mustard seeds, curry leaves, dried red chilli — 3 g
instructions: Heat oil in a kadai, temper mustard seeds, curry leaves and dried red chilli.
Add the boiled chana and toss for 3-4 minutes until well coated.
Stir in grated coconut at the end.
Serve warm as a bowl rather than a small snack portion.
why_it_works: Reframes a traditional snack as a full breakfast portion, not a trivial rename
Very low oil for the protein and fiber delivered
Quick, one-pan preparation

name: ZITLAS Moong Dal Appe
description: A moong dal and semolina batter steamed-fried into small round appe (paniyaram) using a dedicated appe pan — a distinctly different cooking format from a flat crepe.
ingredients: Moong dal, soaked and ground — 70 g
instructions: Mix ground moong dal with rava, onion, carrot and a little water into a thick batter; rest 10 minutes.
Heat the appe pan and add a few drops of oil into each cavity.
Pour batter into each cavity, filling about three-quarters full.
Cover and cook on low heat for 3-4 minutes, then flip each ball gently and cook the other side.
Serve hot with chutney.
why_it_works: Appe format cooks with far less oil than a pan-fried version of the same batter
Small round shape is easy for kids and makes a good family breakfast
Genuinely different mouthfeel — crisp outside, soft inside

name: ZITLAS Oats Besan Dhokla
description: A steamed dhokla batter made with ground oats mixed into besan — a fiber-boosted variation on the classic Gujarati steamed snack.
instructions: Whisk besan, ground oats, curd and water into a smooth, thick-pourable batter.
Add eno fruit salt just before steaming and mix gently until it froths slightly.
Pour into a greased tin and steam in a pressure cooker (without the whistle) for 12-15 minutes.
Cool slightly, cut into squares, and temper with mustard and sesame seeds in hot oil poured over the top.
why_it_works: Oats addition raises fiber meaningfully above a plain besan dhokla
Still steamed, keeping added fat low
Distinct from the plain Besan Dhokla Bites recipe by both ingredient and fiber profile

name: ZITLAS Egg Paneer Combo Bhurji
description: Scrambled egg and crumbled paneer cooked together in one pan — combining two protein sources directly in the bhurji itself, not as separate dishes.
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion and tomato until soft, add turmeric and chilli powder.
Add crumbled paneer and cook 2 minutes.
Beat the egg and pour in, scrambling gently until just set, mixing the paneer through.
Serve hot on its own or with a roti.
why_it_works: Two proteins combined in a single pan rather than served as separate items
Higher protein density than either egg bhurji or paneer bhurji alone
Still a familiar, fast dish to cook

name: ZITLAS Soya Flour Chilla
description: A savoury crepe made from soya flour rather than besan or moong batter — a different protein-forward flour base for people who've had enough besan chilla.
instructions: Whisk soya flour and rice flour with water into a smooth, thin batter.
Mix in onion, cumin seeds and green chilli.
Heat a tawa, pour a ladle of batter and spread thin.
Drizzle a little oil around the edges and cook until crisp on both sides.
Serve with chutney.
why_it_works: Soya flour has a notably higher protein percentage than besan
Different base flour keeps the chilla rotation from feeling repetitive
Very quick, single-pan preparation

name: ZITLAS Roasted Chana Ladoo Bites
description: No-bake bites made from roasted chana flour, jaggery and a little ghee — a besan-free alternative to the peanut chikki bites, portable for a rushed morning.
ingredients: Roasted chana flour (bhuna chana powder) — 100 g
instructions: Melt ghee in a kadai on low heat, add the roasted chana flour and roast for 3-4 minutes until aromatic.
Add jaggery and stir until it melts and combines fully into a thick, moist dough.
Cool slightly, then shape into 8 small balls while still warm.
Store in an airtight container for up to a week.
why_it_works: Different base ingredient from the peanut chikki bites, giving genuine variety among grab-and-go options
Roasted chana flour brings meaningfully more protein than plain flour ladoos
Batch-made once for the whole week

name: ZITLAS Curd Oats Bowl with Roasted Seeds
description: Cold curd mixed with soaked oats and topped with a mix of roasted seeds — a savoury, tangy no-cook bowl distinct from the sweet chia jar or smoothie bowl.
ingredients: Roasted cumin powder, black salt — 2 g
instructions: Soak the oats in a little water for 10 minutes to soften.
Drain any excess water and mix the oats into the curd.
Season with roasted cumin powder and black salt.
Top with mixed roasted seeds just before eating for crunch.
why_it_works: Savoury profile is a genuinely different use of oats from the usual sweet preparations
Seeds on top keep some crunch instead of everything going soft
Zero cooking involved

name: ZITLAS Methi Paneer Paratha
description: A stuffed paratha filled with paneer and fresh fenugreek (methi) leaves — a fiber-and-micronutrient-forward filling distinct from a plain paneer stuffing.
instructions: Mix paneer with chopped methi leaves, ajwain and chilli powder into a filling.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the paneer-methi mixture and seal well.
Roll out gently and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden on both sides.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Methi adds iron and a distinct bitterness that plain paneer parathas don't have
Different vegetable pairing from the Lite Paneer Paratha in Batch 1
Traditional winter-season combination

name: ZITLAS Egg Bhurji Rice Bowl
description: Spiced scrambled egg served over warm rice instead of bread or roti — a rice-bowl format for people who prefer rice at any meal.
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion and tomato until soft, add turmeric and chilli powder.
Beat the egg and pour in, scrambling until just cooked.
Warm the cooked rice separately (or use leftover rice).
Spoon the bhurji over the rice in a bowl and serve.
why_it_works: Rice-bowl format suits users who find bread or roti heavy in the morning
Also works well with leftover rice, doubling as a leftover-friendly option
Quick and familiar flavours in a different presentation

name: ZITLAS Khakhra Peanut Butter Stack
description: Multigrain khakhra crackers spread with peanut butter and stacked — a genuinely no-cook, no-cleanup hostel breakfast using a shelf-stable base.
instructions: Spread peanut butter evenly over each khakhra.
Stack 2-3 khakhras together.
Eat immediately — khakhra stays crisp only briefly once spread.
why_it_works: Both ingredients are shelf-stable, no refrigeration needed at all
Zero cooking, zero cleanup — just a spoon
Genuinely different texture (crisp) from most no-cook options which are soft

name: ZITLAS Steamed Moong Handvo
description: A savoury steamed cake made from ground moong dal, rava and vegetables — a baked/steamed slice format, distinct from any crepe, roll or paratha in the database.
ingredients: Moong dal, soaked and ground — 100 g
Eno fruit salt, mustard seeds — 4 g
instructions: Mix ground moong dal, rava, curd and grated carrot into a thick batter; rest 20 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 180°C and grease a small baking tin.
Add eno fruit salt just before baking and mix gently.
Pour into the tin, temper mustard seeds in hot oil and pour over the top.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until a knife comes out clean.
Cool slightly and cut into slices.
why_it_works: Cake-slice format is genuinely different from every crepe or roll elsewhere in the database
Bakes in one tin with minimal active attention
Good for a family breakfast cut into shared slices

name: ZITLAS Chicken Keema Paratha
description: A stuffed paratha filled with spiced lean chicken mince — a non-vegetarian counterpart to the vegetarian soya keema paratha, using real meat for users who want it.
instructions: Cook the chicken mince with onion, ginger-garlic paste and garam masala in a pan until fully cooked through and fairly dry; cool slightly.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the cooked mince filling and seal well.
Roll out carefully and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden and cooked through on both sides.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Genuine non-vegetarian option for users who prefer real meat over a soya substitute
Lean mince keeps fat moderate while protein stays high
Filling must be fully pre-cooked, which also makes the paratha safer and quicker to roast

name: ZITLAS Oat Flour Paneer Kathi Roll
description: A roti made from oat flour instead of wheat, rolled around a spiced paneer filling kathi-roll style — swaps the base grain rather than the filling.
instructions: Mix oat flour with a small amount of wheat atta (oat flour alone doesn't bind well) and knead into a dough.
Roll out and roast on a tawa until light brown spots appear.
Dry-toss paneer with onion and chaat masala.
Lay the filling on the roti, roll tightly, and serve.
why_it_works: Oat-flour base changes the fiber and glycemic profile of the roti itself, not just the filling
Different construction technique from any other paneer recipe in the database
Still eats like a familiar kathi roll

name: ZITLAS Tofu Ginger-Soy Scramble Wrap
description: Crumbled tofu scrambled with ginger and soy sauce in an Indo-Chinese style, rolled into a wrap — a distinctly different spice profile from the Indian-masala tofu bhurji toast.
instructions: Roll out the atta into a roti and roast on a tawa; keep warm.
Heat oil, saute ginger and garlic, then add crumbled tofu and soy sauce, stirring for 4-5 minutes.
Finish with chopped spring onion.
Spread the tofu scramble onto the roti and roll up tightly.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Indo-Chinese seasoning gives a genuinely different flavour direction from Indian-spiced tofu elsewhere in the database
Fully vegan, high protein
Quick one-pan filling

name: ZITLAS Makhana Peanut Trail Mix Bowl
description: A dry, portable mix of roasted makhana and peanuts with a few raisins — a crunchy grab-and-go bowl distinct from the yogurt-based makhana parfait.
instructions: Combine roasted makhana, peanuts and raisins in a small container.
Mix well.
Carry in the container and eat on the move, or as a sit-down bowl.
why_it_works: Entirely dry format, unlike the yogurt-based makhana parfait, so it travels without spoilage risk
Genuinely no prep beyond mixing
Good option when there's no fridge access

name: ZITLAS Green Moong Soup Bowl
description: A warm, lightly spiced moong dal soup eaten as a savoury liquid breakfast — an unusual soup format rather than a solid dish.
instructions: Pressure cook moong dal with tomato and enough water for 3 whistles until fully soft.
Blend lightly or mash for a smoother, soup-like consistency.
Heat oil, temper cumin seeds and garlic, and pour into the soup.
Season with black pepper and simmer 3-4 minutes.
Serve hot in a mug or bowl, sipped like a soup.
why_it_works: Soup format is genuinely different from every solid breakfast in the database
Very light on the stomach for people who don't want to chew much in the morning
Simple one-pot preparation

name: ZITLAS Paneer Stuffed Idli
description: Regular idli batter poured over a small spiced paneer filling in the mould, so the protein is steamed inside the idli itself rather than served alongside.
instructions: Mix crumbled paneer with chopped coriander and green chilli.
Grease the idli moulds and add a small spoon of batter to each.
Place a small portion of the paneer mixture in the centre, then cover with more batter to fully enclose it.
Steam for 10-12 minutes in a pressure cooker without the whistle.
Serve hot with chutney or sambar.
why_it_works: Protein is steamed inside the idli rather than served as a side, unlike the Protein-Boosted Idli Sambar in Batch 1
Fun surprise-filling format that works well for families and kids too
Still fully steamed, no added oil

name: ZITLAS Vegetable Rava Idli
description: Steamed semolina idli with grated vegetables mixed directly into the batter — no fermentation needed, ready much faster than regular idli.
ingredients: Eno fruit salt, mustard seeds — 4 g
instructions: Dry-roast rava lightly, then mix with curd, grated carrot, peas and a little water into a thick batter; rest 10 minutes.
Add eno fruit salt just before steaming.
Pour into greased idli moulds and steam for 10-12 minutes.
Temper mustard seeds in oil and drizzle over the idlis before serving.
why_it_works: No fermentation wait, so it's ready much faster than dal-based idli
Vegetables mixed directly into the batter, not a side garnish
Distinct base grain from every other idli variant in the database

name: ZITLAS Soya Sabzi Roti Roll
description: A wet, gravy-style soya chunk sabzi rolled inside a roti — distinct from the dry keema-style filling and the frankie's masala-dusted soya.
instructions: Roll out and roast the atta into rotis; keep warm.
Heat oil, saute onion until golden, add ginger-garlic paste and tomato, cook until soft.
Add soya chunks and garam masala with a splash of water, simmer 8-10 minutes into a slightly wet sabzi.
Spoon the sabzi onto a roti and roll (or fold), letting some gravy soak into the bread.
Serve immediately while warm.
why_it_works: Gravy-style filling gives a distinctly different eating experience — softer, saucier — from the other dry soya rolls in the database
Uses the same soya base as other recipes but a genuinely different cooking method
Filling, homely breakfast

name: ZITLAS Curd Rice Balls
description: Portion-sized curd rice shaped into small balls — a portable, lunchbox-ready version of the usual bowl-format curd rice.
instructions: Mash the cold rice with curd until well combined and slightly sticky.
Temper mustard seeds, curry leaves and peanuts in oil and mix into the rice.
Once cool enough to handle, shape into 4-5 small balls.
Pack into a small container — they hold their shape for a few hours.
why_it_works: Ball format is genuinely more portable than the usual curd rice bowl
No last-minute assembly needed once packed
Works well for a mid-morning lunchbox snack rather than a sit-down breakfast

name: ZITLAS Egg Bhurji Pav
description: Mumbai-style spiced scrambled egg stuffed into a soft pav bun — a bun-sandwich format distinct from a roti roll or toast.
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion and tomato until soft, add pav bhaji masala.
Beat the egg and pour in, scrambling until just cooked.
Slice the pav bun and lightly toast the cut sides on the tawa with a touch of butter or oil.
Stuff the egg bhurji into the pav.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Pav bun format is a genuinely different bread base from roti, toast or paratha elsewhere in the database
Mumbai street-food flavour angle keeps the spicing distinct
Fast, familiar comfort food

name: ZITLAS Multi-Millet Savoury Porridge
description: A blended multi-millet flour cooked into a savoury porridge with vegetables — different from any single-millet upma by using a flour blend rather than whole grain.
instructions: Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, then saute finely chopped vegetables for 2-3 minutes.
Add water and bring to a simmer.
Whisk in the multi-millet flour gradually to avoid lumps, stirring continuously.
Simmer 6-8 minutes until it thickens to a porridge consistency, then serve hot.
why_it_works: Flour-blend format cooks faster than whole-grain millet upma
Combines the fiber benefits of several millets rather than just one
Warm, comforting texture for cooler mornings

name: ZITLAS Paneer Palak Toast
description: Mashed paneer mixed with cooked spinach, spread over toasted bread — a green, iron-rich spread format distinct from bhurji or toast dips.
instructions: Heat oil, saute garlic briefly, then add spinach and cook until wilted, about 3 minutes.
Mash the paneer into the cooked spinach, mixing until it forms a spreadable mixture.
Toast the bread slices.
Spread the paneer-palak mixture over the toast and season with black pepper.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Spread format is a genuinely different toast preparation from the besan-battered toast in Batch 1
Spinach adds iron and fiber not present in most other paneer dishes here
Quick and visually different (green) from other toasts

name: ZITLAS Sprout Peanut Salad Cup
description: A no-cook, portion-cup salad of sprouts and crushed peanuts dressed with lemon — packed the night before for a genuinely zero-morning-effort breakfast.
instructions: Rinse and drain the sprouts well.
Toss with crushed peanuts, lemon juice and chaat masala.
Pack into a sealed cup or container the night before.
Eat straight from the container in the morning — no reheating or assembly needed.
why_it_works: Explicitly designed to be assembled the night before, unlike other no-cook recipes eaten immediately
Zero morning effort at all beyond opening the container
Very low cost, very portable

name: ZITLAS Baked Sweet Potato with Curd
description: An oven-baked sweet potato split open and topped with curd and crushed peanuts — a grain-free breakfast base built around a root vegetable instead.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C and bake the whole sweet potato for 20-25 minutes until soft when pierced.
Split it open lengthwise.
Top with curd and crushed peanuts.
Sprinkle chaat masala and serve warm.
why_it_works: Genuinely grain-free breakfast base, unusual in an Indian breakfast context
Sweet potato brings fiber and beta-carotene that grain bases don't
Very simple, mostly hands-off oven cooking

name: ZITLAS Egg Curry Rice Bowl
description: A rice bowl topped with the same light egg curry used in the roti version, but served over rice instead — a distinct pairing from the Egg Curry with Multigrain Roti recipe.
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion until golden, add ginger-garlic paste and tomato, cook until pulpy.
Add garam masala and a little water to form a light gravy; simmer 5 minutes.
Halve the boiled eggs and simmer in the gravy for 2-3 minutes.
Serve the egg curry ladled over warm rice in a bowl.
why_it_works: Rice-bowl pairing is a genuinely different meal format from the roti version, suiting rice-preference households
Same curry technique reused efficiently, but the eating experience differs meaningfully
One-pan gravy, minimal cleanup

name: ZITLAS Chana Chaat Toast
description: A tangy boiled-chana chaat piled directly onto toasted bread — combines a chaat and a toast into one dish rather than serving them separately.
instructions: Toast the bread slices lightly.
Toss boiled chana with onion, tomato, lemon juice and chaat masala in a bowl.
Pile the chana chaat generously onto the toast.
Eat immediately with a fork before the toast softens.
why_it_works: Combining chaat and toast into one dish is a distinct format from either eaten separately
High fiber and protein for very low cost
Fast to assemble with almost no active cooking

name: ZITLAS Moong Cheela Mini Pizza
description: A moong dal cheela base topped like a mini pizza with tomato, onion, capsicum and grated paneer, then briefly covered to melt — a playful, family-friendly format.
ingredients: Moong dal, soaked and ground — 60 g
instructions: Cook the moong dal batter into a thick round cheela base on the tawa, as usual, but only on one side.
Flip so the uncooked side faces up, then scatter tomato, capsicum and grated paneer over the top.
Cover with a lid and cook on low heat for 3-4 minutes so the toppings soften and the paneer softens slightly.
Sprinkle oregano and chilli flakes, slice like a pizza, and serve.
why_it_works: Playful topped format makes it distinctly different from a folded or rolled cheela
Kid-friendly presentation without losing the protein content
One pan, no oven needed unlike a real pizza

name: ZITLAS Soya Stuffed Pav
description: Spiced soya granules stuffed into a pav bun, Mumbai vada-pav-style but with soya replacing the usual potato filling.
ingredients: Mustard seeds, turmeric, green chilli — 3 g
instructions: Heat oil, temper mustard seeds, add onion and green chilli, saute until soft.
Add rehydrated soya granules and turmeric, cook 4-5 minutes until well coated and slightly dry.
Slice the pav and lightly toast the cut sides.
Stuff the soya mixture generously into the pav.
Serve with a side of green chutney.
why_it_works: Familiar vada-pav format but with a higher-protein, lower-oil filling than the traditional potato vada
Different bread base from any roti-based soya recipe in the database
Genuinely street-food-inspired without deep frying

name: ZITLAS Ragi Malt Drink
description: A traditional Karnataka-style fermented-style ragi malt porridge drink, sipped from a glass — a liquid finger-millet format distinct from ragi dosa or rajgira porridge.
instructions: Whisk ragi flour into a little cold water to avoid lumps.
Bring the rest of the water to a boil, add the ragi mixture, and simmer 6-8 minutes, stirring often, until it thickens slightly and loses its raw smell.
Cool to room temperature, then whisk in buttermilk and cumin powder.
Pour into a glass and drink — this is a savoury, sippable porridge, not a thick bowl.
why_it_works: Liquid, sippable format is distinct from every solid ragi or millet dish in the database
Very cooling and light, suited to hot mornings
Traditional South Indian drink genuinely different from a smoothie

name: ZITLAS Paneer Bhurji Kulcha
description: Spiced paneer bhurji stuffed inside a kulcha instead of a roti or paratha — a different bread base with its own texture and flavour.
instructions: Knead refined flour with curd and a little water into a soft kulcha dough; rest 15 minutes.
Mix paneer with onion and chaat masala for the filling.
Roll out the dough, stuff with the paneer filling and seal.
Roast on a hot tawa with a little oil until golden with brown spots on both sides.
Serve hot with pickle.
why_it_works: Kulcha dough (with curd) has a distinctly softer, richer texture from a plain wheat roti or paratha
Different bread technique broadens the database's bread formats beyond roti/paratha
Restaurant-style comfort food made at home

name: ZITLAS Leftover Rice Egg Fried Rice Bowl
description: Leftover rice and egg stir-fried Indo-Chinese style with vegetables — a genuinely different leftover-rice recipe from the Maharashtrian-style protein poha version in Batch 1.
ingredients: Soy sauce, garlic, spring onion — 6 g
instructions: Heat oil in a kadai on high heat, saute garlic and vegetables for 2 minutes.
Push to one side, crack in the egg and scramble it in the empty space.
Add the cold leftover rice and soy sauce, tossing everything together on high heat for 3-4 minutes.
Finish with chopped spring onion and serve hot.
why_it_works: Indo-Chinese flavour direction is genuinely different from the tempered, turmeric-based leftover rice poha in Batch 1
High-heat tossing gives a different texture (slightly charred) from a softer poha-style dish
Uses cold rice specifically, working better than fresh rice for this technique

name: ZITLAS Curd Chilla
description: A besan chilla batter enriched with whisked curd for extra protein and a softer texture — a variant that changes the batter itself, not the filling.
instructions: Whisk besan with curd, water, turmeric and cumin seeds into a smooth batter (curd replaces some of the water used in a plain chilla).
Mix in chopped onion.
Heat a tawa, pour a ladle of batter and spread into a round.
Drizzle a little oil and cook until golden on both sides.
Serve with chutney.
why_it_works: Curd in the batter itself raises protein above a plain besan chilla without adding a separate filling step
Softer, slightly tangier texture than the usual water-based chilla
Still a one-pan, quick preparation

name: ZITLAS Boiled Egg Curry Wrap
description: A drier version of egg curry, thickened and reduced, wrapped inside a roti instead of eaten with rice or a separate roti — a wrap format for the same base curry technique.
instructions: Roll out and roast the atta into a roti; keep warm.
Heat oil, saute onion until golden, add ginger-garlic paste and tomato, cook until dry and thick (less liquid than the bowl versions).
Chop the boiled eggs and mix into the thick masala, coating well without excess gravy.
Spoon onto the roti and roll tightly so it doesn't leak.
Wrap in foil and serve.
why_it_works: Deliberately drier consistency than the two curry-bowl versions, specifically so it holds together as a wrap
Third genuinely different way to eat the same egg-curry base across the database — bowl with roti, bowl with rice, and now a wrap
Portable for a commute

name: ZITLAS Matki Usal Bowl
description: A Maharashtrian-style sprouted moth bean (matki) usal, tempered and simmered — using a legume not used elsewhere in the database for genuine protein-source diversity.
ingredients: Goda masala or garam masala — 4 g
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion until golden, add tomato and cook until soft.
Add the boiled sprouted matki and goda masala, mixing well.
Add a little water and simmer 6-8 minutes until the flavours combine.
Serve hot as a bowl, with a squeeze of lemon if liked.
why_it_works: Matki is a distinct legume from moong, chana or rajma already used across the database
Traditional Maharashtrian usal reframed as a protein-forward breakfast rather than a side dish
One-pan, genuinely regional

name: ZITLAS Paneer Corn Tikki
description: Pan-fried patties combining crumbled paneer with boiled corn kernels — a distinct filling combination from any other tikki or cutlet in the database.
instructions: Mash paneer with boiled corn, onion, coriander and green chilli into a coarse mixture.
Shape into 3-4 small tikkis.
Pan-fry in oil until golden on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Serve with mint chutney.
why_it_works: Corn adds natural sweetness and a distinct texture not present in other tikki recipes here
Kid-friendly flavour profile suits family breakfasts
Different filling combination from the sprout-paneer or moong-dal tikkis

name: ZITLAS No-Bake Atta Ladoo Bites
description: No-bake bites made from roasted whole wheat flour, ghee and jaggery — a wheat-based grab-and-go option distinct from the chana-flour and peanut versions.
instructions: Roast the atta in ghee on low heat for 8-10 minutes, stirring continuously, until it turns golden and smells nutty.
Add jaggery and mix until it melts in fully.
Cool slightly, then shape into 8 small balls while still warm.
Store in an airtight container for up to a week.
why_it_works: Third distinct base flour among the ladoo-style bites in the database (wheat, not besan or chana flour)
Very low ingredient count, easy to batch cook
Traditional winter combination made portion-sized

name: ZITLAS Soya Milk Ragi Porridge
description: Ragi flour cooked into a warm porridge using soya milk instead of dairy milk — a fully vegan pairing distinct from the dairy-based rajgira porridge.
instructions: Whisk ragi flour into a little cold soya milk to avoid lumps.
Heat the rest of the soya milk, add the ragi mixture and stir continuously.
Simmer 6-8 minutes until thickened.
Stir in jaggery and cardamom powder, cook 1-2 more minutes, and serve warm.
why_it_works: Fully dairy-free pairing, unlike the milk-based Rajgira Milk Porridge earlier in this batch
Ragi's calcium content pairs well with soya milk's protein for a vegan-complete combination
Good option for lactose-intolerant users

name: ZITLAS Leftover Dal Rice Cutlets
description: Leftover toor dal and leftover rice mashed together and shaped into pan-fried cutlets — rescues two different leftovers at once in a single dish.
instructions: Mash the leftover dal and rice together with onion and spices.
Add a little rice flour if the mixture feels too wet to hold shape.
Shape into small cutlets.
Pan-fry in oil until crisp and golden on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Serve with ketchup or chutney.
why_it_works: Rescues two separate leftovers — dal and rice — in one dish, unlike single-leftover recipes elsewhere in the database
Crisping via pan-frying gives a genuinely different texture from just reheating either leftover
Very low additional cost since the base is already cooked

name: ZITLAS Greek Yogurt Chilla Crumble Bowl
description: A besan chilla is torn into pieces and layered into a bowl with Greek yogurt and chutney, deconstructed rather than served as a whole crepe.
instructions: Whisk besan with water and cumin seeds into a batter and cook a thin chilla on a tawa as usual.
Once cooked, tear the chilla into bite-sized pieces rather than rolling or folding it.
Layer the torn chilla pieces in a bowl with Greek yogurt and a drizzle of mint chutney.
Mix gently just before eating, like a deconstructed chaat.
why_it_works: Deconstructed bowl format is a genuinely different eating experience from every rolled or folded chilla elsewhere in the database
Greek yogurt adds meaningfully more protein than curd would
Fun, chaat-like way to eat a familiar base
